discovery.canonical_face_rule: per study, the dated build; the *_latest twin is dropped
discovery.prose_rule: every other .json mention is reported and never counted
discovery.row_pointer_rule: a .json string whose immediate parent key is one of face,face_file,face_name,face_path,faces,file,path,source,source_face,src or whose parent container key contains 'face'

forward_vintage_rows.note: counted face carries a later stamp than the census face

identity_checks.check: every census has at least one counted study
covered + missed equals the census edge count
census edge count equals the sum of per-row counted censuses
the vintage audit covers every census edge
declared kind counts sum to the census rows
prose mentions are never folded into rows
the study's own face is not in the discovery set

notes: A census is defined by what it does, not by its name: a study counts as a census only when its face carries a structured row pointer to another study's face. Prose mentions are published in prose_only_targets and are never counted.
The declared guard on every face is `self_faces_excluded`, and on 10 of 31 censuses it names only that face's own two filenames -- a list that cannot answer 'is this face itself a census'.

E317 is the only face that declares a filename-prefix family list; it still counts censuses outside that list, so the list is a copy of the writer's recent family rather than a property of the population.
Filenames are not versions: a census row names a file, and that file is rewritten in place, so the content a census actually counted is not recoverable from the arc.
Vintage comparison is granularity-aware: a date-only stamp against a same-day timestamp is INDETERMINATE, never forward. Plain string comparison manufactures 34 extra forward edges on this face.
title: which study faces are counted as rows by later censuses of the same programme, and is the exclusion list a declared property or a copy of the writer's own family
